answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock stake in a dynamic registry where minting identities burns tokens at a superlinear cost of $O(n^2)$. Much like dredging a vast ocean bed, extracting ferrous ore, or carving tunnels through solid karst rock, expanding artificial clusters imposes quadratic economic friction. By enforcing verifiable cryptographic stake burning per node, an attacker facing superlinear scaling incurs prohibitive capital depletion.
